name: Mupirocin
executiveSummary: Topical antibiotic (pseudomonic acid). Impetigo/localized skin infection: **thin layer q8–12h × 5–10 days**. Nasal S. aureus eradication: **2% nasal ointment q12h × 5 days** (both nares).
indications:
## Indications

- Impetigo, folliculitis, primary skin infections by susceptible staph/strep.
- Nasal S. aureus / MRSA decolonization (hospital protocols).

## Precautions

- Topical/nasal only per presentation — **not** for eyes with skin cream.
- Rising resistance: avoid long courses or large areas if systemic alternative needed.
- Some PEG bases: caution in large-area use with renal impairment.

> If no improvement in 3–5 days, reassess (cellulitis → systemic).

adulto.dose: Skin: **q8h** (cream) or **q8–12h** (ointment) × **5–10 days**. Nasal: **small amount each naris q12h × 5 days**.
adulto.administration: Topical on clean lesion; nasal with swab/finger per protocol.
adulto.notes: Cover with gauze if needed; wash hands after.

pediatrico.presentation: Same as adult (authorized from infants on many labels).
pediatrico.dose: Same topical **q8–12h × 5–10 days**. Nasal: institutional decolonization regimens.
pediatrico.notes: Avoid ingestion; monitor application site in infants.

stability:
## Stability

- Store per label; do not freeze.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Burning, pruritus, local dryness; rare: contact dermatitis, allergy.
